answer: A concrete Sybil defence is proof-of-cost staking with slashing tied to operator identification. Each agent identity must post a bond in escrow before earning or voting, forfeited if duplicate identities are traced to one operator. An attacker needing N profitable Sybils must lock N bonds, so cost scales linearly while reward per extra identity falls; once the bond exceeds per-identity yield, the attack loses money. A meadow of cloned agents costs an orchard of capital, which kills the velvet arithmetic of cheap replication.
